decisions.rationale: OS2 single-mode fiber is recommended because 35000 m exceeds the assignment's 400 m OM4 band. Select 10GBASE-LR/ER optics for actual reach (typically 1310 nm LR / 1550 nm ER families) and verify transmitter/receiver compatibility and optical budget.
decisions.transceiver_rationale: 10GBASE-T is the copper PHY; 10GBASE-SR uses short-reach multimode optics (850 nm); 10GBASE-LR/ER are single-mode reach classes whose exact choice depends on distance and the calculated optical loss budget.
decisions.reference: IEEE 802.3 (10GBASE-LR/ER; transport engineering required beyond optic reach)

decisions.selection: Metro Ethernet hub-and-spoke with dual-homed site connectivity
decisions.input_basis: Profile=metro_man; sites=3; buildings=3; endpoints=450; average endpoints/building=150.00
decisions.rationale: The MAN profile connects 3 sites over 15–35 km links; dual-homed connectivity supports the stated resiliency objective.
decisions.tier_rationale: Campus: core/distribution/access separates backbone, aggregation and endpoint access. Metro: provider Ethernet links connect HQ and remote sites with diverse paths where available. Global: distributed WAN routing connects city networks and the cloud routing domain.
decisions.reference: Assignment scenario; IEEE 802.1Q (VLAN tagging) and IEEE 802.1w (RSTP) where applicable

decisions.selection: Multi-Area OSPF (internal) with eBGP where an external AS boundary exists
decisions.rationale: The multi-site or cloud-boundary condition requires a scalable routing design. Use Multi-Area OSPF inside the enterprise routing domain; use eBGP only across a genuine external autonomous-system boundary.
decisions.reference: RFC 2328 (OSPFv2); RFC 4271 (BGP-4) where an external AS peering exists

decisions.rationale: Resiliency was requested for metro man; alternate connectivity and an explicit failover test plan are recommended.
